title: A Soft Beginning
author: Gregorian
blurb: The two long central words, if solved at once, will give sufficient clues to permit of rapid solution.

title: Try And Do It
author: W. W. Foster
blurb: This enigma comes from New London, where they specialize in regattas, which is the one unusual word omitted from Mr. Foster's contraption.

title: A Simplicity
author: Isidore Edelstein
blurb: , points of the compass and so on. It is not the purest usage, but may be passed to get over a difficult spot.

title: Tetracruciform
author: Charles W. Snizek
blurb: A mystical design combined with everyday words shorter than the name it it bears.

title: Well Balanced
author: Mr. and Mrs. H. C. Waller
blurb: This is a nice study in words of medium length, as was dictated by the two-ply "X" construction.

title: Baby Grand Model
author: Helen V. Christ
blurb: Only two long words. This should be pie for the hard-boiled solvers and a pleasant exercise for the beginner.

title: A Four Petaled Rose
author: M. Francis Cavallon, Jr.
blurb: Mostly short words, and not difficult. Good corner masses. Mr.

title: A Spotted Border
author: E. Pinkerton
blurb: This puzzle possesses the merit of an interesting double central interlock.

title: A Checkered Career
author: S. Czurles
blurb: Odd words and even. But good practice for the tough ones coming later on.

title: Small But Neat
author: Joseph E. Austrian
blurb: Eight unkeyed letters, but on the whole a very good design. Excellent corner interlock.

title: Keys And Crosses
author: Harold McKay
blurb: The design of this bath mat is much more cryptic than the words you will be called upon to fill in.

title: A Black Beauty
author: P. B. Geotsch
blurb: Anyone who geotsch this one is good. This one shows how hard it is to solve a puzzle with many unkeyed letters.

title: A Grand Old Puzzle
author: Sylvan L. Froelich
blurb: There are some grand old words in this puzzle, and the interlock is something grand also.

title: A Quadripuntal Asteroid
author: Persephone
blurb: A brilliant construction, comprising clever interlocking combined with symmetry of design.

title: A Quadruplix Quiddity
author: Person or Persons Unknown
blurb: A truly marvelous study in four-letter words, with some notably lengthy side-interlocks. The unknown author is to be congratulated.

title: A Well-tied Sailor's Knot
author: Captain F. F. Stewart
blurb: The sea contributes a spacious, ample field of voyage. It is remarkable for the presence of no small units -- two or three letter words.

title: A Tesselated Tangle
author: Persephone
blurb: Perfect interlocking and very few unkeyed letters! Technically, this puzzle is nearly perfect.

title: Hot Cross Buns
author: Everett A. Brown
blurb: This cookie will put you in a Brown study. The 32 horizontal is to 20 vertical and not to 61 horizontal.

title: Stepping Stones
author: D. Weiner
blurb: This looks like a rocky road. Don't trip over it.

title: Five Greek Crosses
author: William Ziegler
blurb: Four interesting, independent masses with a solid central interlock. This is the kind that leads you merrily on from one section to another.

title: At The Crossroads
author: Helen V. Christ
blurb: Small, but plenty of unusual words to tax the lobes of your brain and the pages of your dictionary. Do you like difficult words?

title: Crossword Valentine
author: J. W. Shaw
blurb: This contributor has dedicated himself to romance. We wish we knew the lady to whom he devoted this valentine.

title: Eighteen Karat
author: Harry Friedman
blurb: The author, a jeweler of Maiden Lane, dragged this from his treasure chest. After you do it, you'll agree it's a gem.

title: Honeymoon Hokum
author: Mr. and Mrs. William Stern II
blurb: They constructed this on their honeymoon, which is a good argument for marriage.

title: For The Zigzag Zealot
author: Joseph H. Gersten
blurb: This pattern zigs itself one way and zags itself the other way. Even the most zealous will find some unusual words.

title: This Takes The Cake
author: M. H. Ronzone
blurb: Cut yourself a piece of this one. It's a mouthful. A fine mixture of long and short words.

title: A Jersey 'Skeeter
author: Henry Kroener
blurb: This comes from Montclair, and it'll sting you more than once. Get out the citronella and go to it.

title: Unlucky
author: Harold H. Hodges
blurb: There are thirteen crosses in this widget and the words around them will make you the same.

title: Single Spotter
author: J. T. Delaney
blurb: Not so decorative, but a hundred per cent interlock and no two letter words. Hats off to Mr. Delaney.

title: A Prize Package
author: H. R. Koegler
blurb: The six, seven and nine letter words in this scintillating set-up will tax your gray matter, if any.

title: Hic Labor Hic Opus Est
author: Neophyte
blurb: This erudite contribution comes from an old-time puzzler who is one of the experts on ingenuities.

title: A Serrate Syzygy
author: Marcam
blurb: Another of Marcam's masterpieces, somewhat simpler of solution than her other effort.

title: A Slotted Oblong
author: Marion Hague
blurb: Splendid corner solids and easy central islands. Good words. A nice one to solve at leisure.

title: An Hour Glass
author: Mrs. Henry Wolf
blurb: The constructor must have turned her hour glass several times while she was building this hour glass.

title: Decoration
author: Anna J. Munro
blurb: A good deal of black, but very ornamental. The center, with its outreaching arms, is well built.

title: Black Beetle
author: Fred L. Kleinschmidt
blurb: This constructor blocked out a pretty fair beetle form. The center is a little loose.

title: Facile Est Decensus Averni
author: Cerberus
blurb: Cerberus was a three-faced dog, and that is what you may think of the progenitors of this bark after you've tried it.

title: A West Pointer
author: Corporal Arthur Baisch and Sergeant William M. Munroe
blurb: The army sends a neat design -- and not an easy one.

title: Not So Black As Painted
author: Norman Kendy
blurb: Excellent center, but somewhat loose corner construction, passed, however, under Mr.

title: Fine And Dandy
author: Julie D. Carder
blurb: A splendid example of what can be done in the waving of long and intricate word patterns.

title: A Lingual Labyrinth
author: Coutance
blurb: This effort contains one definition which comprises two words, but the all-round excellence of the construction makes up for this single deficiency.

title: A Hundred Per Center
author: R. and R. Williams
blurb: This is the simplest form for securing an all-over interlock with no unkeyed letters. And the words are good!

title: Crank Her Up
author: Frank A. Ford
blurb: In spite of much black and a complicated design, which compels the use of some unkeyed letters, this puzzle gets by with colors flying.

title: Vocabulary Tester
author: Irvan Neckerman
blurb: Mr. Neckerman is apparently never happy till he has filled his construction with difficult words.

title: In Words of One Syllable
author: J. T. Delaney
blurb: Ever read a book in words of one syllable? This has no higher percentage of polysyllabic words than that.

title: Of Somewhat Oriental Flavor
author: Gregorian
blurb: An excellent construction, admirable chiefly for the entire absence of two-letter words and for the central interlock.
